title: Apple as a Diversification Play Amidst AI Spending Concerns
description: Many US tech giants are investing heavily in AI, leading to significant capital expenditure and potential risks for investors. Apple, in contrast, has maintai.

faq.q: Why is Apple considered a diversification play amidst AI spending?
faq.a: Apple has a more diversified business model across hardware, software, and services, with a comparatively lower capital expenditure than other tech giants heavily invested in AI infrastructure. This offers tech exposure with a different risk profile.

faq.q: What is the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)?
faq.a: The LRS allows resident Indian individuals to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year for various purposes, including overseas investments in shares and mutual funds. (Source: RBI)

faq.q: How are dividends from US stocks taxed for Indian investors?
faq.a: Dividends from US stocks are subject to a 25% withholding tax in the US. Under the India-US DTAA, Indian investors can claim a tax credit for this amount when filing their income tax returns in India.

faq.q: Are capital gains on US stocks taxed in the US for Indian residents?
faq.a: Generally, capital gains on the sale of US stocks are taxed only in India for Indian residents, as per the DTAA, provided you furnish a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the US tax authorities.

faq.q: What is the holding period for long-term capital gains on US stocks in India?
faq.a: To qualify as long-term capital gains (LTCG) in India, US stocks must be held for more than 24 months. Gains from sales within 24 months are considered short-term capital gains (STCG).

faq.q: How does currency fluctuation affect returns from US stock investments?
faq.a: Currency fluctuations can significantly impact your returns. If the Indian Rupee depreciates against the US Dollar, your returns in INR terms will increase, and vice-versa, when you convert your investment back to INR.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of investing in Apple from India, particularly regarding LRS limits and DTAA. However, some tax details, especially the LTCG rate and indexation benefit, are outdated or incorrect based on recent budget changes.

corrections.note: Corrected Apple's capital expenditure and stock performance figures for 2023, and updated the information regarding long-term capital gains taxation for US stocks for Indian residents, specifically the applicability of indexation benefit for sales on or after July 23, 2024.
